prompts: Use case: scientific-educational. Create a landscape Study Buddy infographic for Analysis Reporting Lesson 2.3. Title exactly 'A chart answers a question. An infographic explains a message.' Adult learning design, warm white background, navy text, muted teal and restrained amber, generous spacing and very readable English. Two related panels: left 'Chart' with a simple generic unnumbered chart icon and labels 'Focused comparison', 'Readable labels and units', 'Clear source and context'; right 'Infographic' with a page-like visual story containing labelled elements 'Headline', 'Context', 'Evidence', 'Explanation', 'Limits and sources'. A central connector says 'A chart can be part of an infographic'. Bottom note exactly 'Both can stand alone when their message and context are clear.' Footer exactly 'Design supports understanding. It must not distort the evidence.' Do not imply every chart needs spoken commentary, every infographic requires multiple charts, or that either format guarantees comprehension. No actual statistical values, dataset findings, software screenshots, real logos or completion marks.

Use case: scientific-educational. Create a landscape Study Buddy infographic for Analysis Reporting Task 2.3. Title exactly 'From Kaggle data to a GIMP infographic'. Adult study design, warm white, navy, muted teal and restrained amber, highly readable English. Seven numbered steps with small conceptual icons: '1 Choose a Kaggle dataset', '2 Inspect it in Excel', '3 Explore and verify', '4 Plan the message', '5 Build GIMP layers', '6 Check sources and readability', '7 Save XCF and export JPEG'. In a separate file-output panel show two distinct document icons labelled 'Editable project .xcf' and 'Final image .jpg'. Callout exactly '800 × 1200 px is an example, not a fixed requirement.' Footer exactly 'Use your own EDA findings. Cite data and external visuals.' Show an empty evidence card labelled 'Question · Measure · Chart · Finding · Limit'. No fabricated data or findings, no fake GIMP interface, no claim of a completed student project, no ready-to-submit image, no source statistics or car-sales scenario.
